From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Cc: 
Date: 2028-09-18T10:02:00-07:00
Subject: Runway scenarios: capacity sensitivity matrix for QBR

Team —

We need a crisp set of deliverables for next week’s leadership QBR: a capacity sensitivity matrix that ties utilization scenarios to expected GPU spend, and a short one-page unit-econ summary for execs. Key asks: 

- Build a scenario matrix (Baseline / Surge / 2-week Spike / Worst-case) with: expected slot utilization, actual QPS per model mix, and resulting monthly GPU spend.
- Produce a unit economics table: cost per token (by model class / quantization), effective cost per active session, and sensitivity to batching and KV caching.
- Show where autoscale and pre-warm slots change peak spend (include pre-warm cost vs. cold-start SLA risk).
- Call out vendor/hardware assumptions (A100 / H100 perf and per-hour cost).

Deliverables by 2028-09-20 EOD: 1) capacity-scenarios.xlsx (template attached), 2) sensitivity-matrix.csv, 3) one-page unit-econ summary and a 3-slide executive blurb for the QBR deck.

I attached the template to speed things up. Please flag any missing inputs — Lauren, can you own the QBR blurb and final slide? Markus and Karthik, you own the matrix and orchestration assumptions. Rishi, can you finalize unit-econ numbers and combine into the slide pack?

Thanks — short and tactical.

— Marissa
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Ops, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
(attachment: capacity-scenarios.xlsx)

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-19T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway scenarios: capacity sensitivity matrix for QBR

Uploading the first-pass sensitivity outputs (attached as sensitivity-matrix.csv). High-level notes: 

- Batching impact: across conversational loads we've seen 15–30% per-token cost reduction as utilization moves from 30% -> 70% due to larger mean batch sizes. At 95th percentile spikes batching gains compress (less headroom), so show both median and 95th effects.
- KV cache: for multi-turn chat workloads, prefix cache reduces redundant token compute by ~22% on average (assumes 3-turn median session). Cache hit rate sensitivity included in sheet.
- Hardware assumptions: A100 baseline perf, H100 best-case perf. For rough numbers: A100 effective token throughput = X (normalized), H100 = ~1.35x; include cloud list price per GPU-hour in the matrix.
- Pre-warm slots: reduce tail latency SLA failures by ~85% for warm sessions but add ~6–12% steady-state spend depending on slot life.

I annotated the CSV with the formulas and scenario toggles. Will iterate on numbers if Rishi wants different cost inputs.

(attachment: sensitivity-matrix.csv)
— Markus
Markus Klein
Director, Infrastructure Economics

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-19T14:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Runway scenarios: capacity sensitivity matrix for QBR

Marked up with orchestration implications:

- Slot sizing: recommend two slot families: small (for embeddings/light inferencing) and large (for chat/long context). Map the scenario matrix into slot mix percentages and show impact on utilization.
- Autoscale policy: use conservative cooldowns on surge scenarios to avoid oscillation; when modeling surge, include a 10–15 minute ramp with burst pool (cold-start penalty baked in).
- Cost knobs to highlight to leadership: batching, cache TTL tuning, and pre-warm counts — show a short-run vs long-run spend comparison for each knob.

I'll add a short appendix on orchestration risk (race conditions during scale down) that we can include if leadership asks deeper operational questions.

— Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Engineering Manager, Orchestration

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-09-20T09:40:00-07:00
Subject: Unit econ summary + slides (first pass)

Folks — attached is a consolidated unit-econ summary and a first-pass slide PDF for the QBR. Highlights:

- Expected baseline monthly GPU spend (mixed model mix): $1.28M; surge scenario (30% extra traffic) pushes to ~$1.68M.
- Batching sensitivity: moving to aggressive batching settings (increase batch window from 20ms -> 40ms) drops token unit cost by ~18% but increases median latency by ~12ms; present both in the slide.
- Cache sensitivity: a +10% cache hit-rate improvement saves ~$85k/mo in medium workloads.
- Recommendation: for the QBR ask leadership for conditional approval to pre-warm ~8% of slots during expected Q4 peaks (estimated incremental cost ~$45k/mo) to keep SLAs without sacrificing unit economics.

Please review the CSV and PDF and flag any numbers that look off. If no pushback, I'll merge into final deck and prepare the CFO-facing one-liner.

(attachments: unit-econ-summary.csv, qbr-presentation-draft.pdf)

— Rishi
Rishi Malhotra
VP, Platform Finance

Michael — forwarding our internal QBR prep so you can validate the assumptions that affect your Q4 capacity and costs. Short asks for Nimbus Health: 

1) Confirm expected peak concurrent sessions and any known campaign dates in Q4 (even ranges are fine).
2) Procurement — are there limits on committed monthly spend or consent to our recommended pre-warm slot approach? We estimate a modest incremental spend (~$45k/mo) to keep latency SLAs during peak windows.
3) Any constraints on using H100-class instances in your region? If not, we’ll show a best/worst case in the deck.

Attachments are included in the Drive folder here (same link): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2Bq-QBR-Runway-2028

If you can reply by 2028-09-22 EOD that would let us finalize the CFO slide.

Best —
Marissa
